scope: Confirmatory retrieval gate and one strict common live form comparison.

spec.brief: A tenant needs to report a broken common-area light. Collect building, location and a description, and offer Routine and Safety issue as urgency options. Make it usable by keyboard and show that the request was prepared locally after valid submission.
spec.task: Use the keyboard to try submitting with the required data empty. Note the actionable message or browser validation and where focus lands. Then enter Oak Court as the building, Second-floor landing as the location, and Common-area light is out as the description. Verify that Routine and Safety issue are available. Select Safety issue and submit. Verify that the visible confirmation says the request was prepared locally and check focus and any available return action. Report any differences from the exact brief. At 390 px, check for horizontal scrolling or obscured feedback. Capture -before on entry, -edge where the invalid submission is visible, and -after once a real valid submission has reached confirmation. After the confirmation capture, return to the form with the keyboard and check that Oak Court, the landing, the description, and Safety issue are retained.

shadcn.evidence_rule: A successful read-only call must actually return an exact registered official name before the HTML reply. Query echoes and empty code examples do not qualify.

preregistration.comparison_scope: Frozen Design MCP and UI UX Pro Max controls against a fresh shadcn generation with the same sealed prompt.
preregistration.visual_gate: Anonymous 1440 and 390 pixel views, 3 captures each, real keyboard and exact task facts.

prompt:
Build the UI in the brief below. Produce one complete HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript. Return it in a single html code fence. Keep interactions local and use only the supplied facts. Google Fonts stylesheets are allowed. Use original inline illustrations or CSS for visuals. Do not use other remote assets, imports, or calls. The review runs in Chrome at widths of 1440 and 390 pixels. Before writing HTML, retrieve relevant design context through your connected tool. For direct pass the brief verbatim as brief. For design_guidance pass the brief verbatim as query with design_system=true. For component registries retrieve one relevant component or example with a short component name. Use the returned guidance. If you cannot get a relevant result, stop. Do not write files or call other tools.

Brief:
A tenant needs to report a broken common-area light. Collect building, location and a description, and offer Routine and Safety issue as urgency options. Make it usable by keyboard and show that the request was prepared locally after valid submission.

calibration.reason: Clear labels and legibility support the task, but the familiar layout is not distinctive and misplaced focus impedes error recovery.

primary_action.input: Keyboard: enter Oak Court, Second-floor landing and Common-area light is out; select Safety issue with the arrow key; submit.
primary_action.expected: A locally prepared confirmation with the entered details and a return action.
primary_action.observed: Confirmation says the request was prepared locally and not sent; all four values appear. Focus moves to the confirmation heading. Tab and Enter on Edit request return to the form with all values retained.

A-1440.edge_observation: Empty submission shows actionable messages for all three text fields and moves focus to Building. Routine is initially selected; Safety issue is available.
A-1440.fact_check: The visible confirmation meets the local-preparation wording. The claim that data stays local was not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: Clear two-column hierarchy, helpful location guidance and a readable confirmation summary.
A-1440.weakness: The illustration and rounded form treatment are pleasant but familiar.
A-1440.repair: Give the lighting illustration a more distinctive relationship to the task.
